entries.clue: Primarily squalid purveyor, illicit vendor? (4)

indicatorNotes.Primarily: 'primarily' means first of all, so take the first letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of Squalid, Purveyor, Illicit, Vendor

annotation.surface: A description of a shady street trader selling dodgy goods.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: its initials spell the answer and its words describe him. A spiv is British slang for a flashy petty crook dealing in black-market goods.
annotation.definitionFit: A spiv is a small-time dealer in illicit or black-market goods.

entries.clue: I reopened bananas and showed the way (9)

indicatorNotes.bananas: 'bananas' means crazy, so the letters go wild

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone opened up a bunch of bananas again and led by example.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like the fruit being reopened, but it is the slang for mad, telling you to scramble 'I reopened'.
annotation.definitionFit: To pioneer something is to be first, showing others the way.

entries.clue: Victor is constant, on time, showing guts (7)

blocks.note: Victor is V in the NATO alphabet
used as is
c is the constant for the speed of light
an era is a period of time; 'on' puts it after

annotation.surface: A man called Victor keeps showing courage, always on time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guts' in the surface means courage, but the definition wants the literal innards.
annotation.definitionFit: Viscera are the internal organs of the body, the guts.

entries.clue: Tiny amount of drink – damn! (4)

blocks.note: a tiny splash added to a glass, as with soda
a mild, old-fashioned British oath standing in for 'damn!'

annotation.surface: Someone curses on finding only a drop left in the glass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dash!' is an old-fashioned, polite British substitute for 'damn!'.
annotation.definitionFit: A dash is a small splash of liquid, and 'dash!' is a genteel curse.

entries.clue: Gather intel from – scare the pants off? (7)

blocks.note: to question an agent after a mission
read literally: remove someone's briefs, i.e. underpants, as a prefix DE- would

annotation.surface: A spy interrogation that aims to terrify the subject.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is a pun: 'pants' are underpants in Britain, and briefs are underpants, so taking them off is to de-brief.
annotation.definitionFit: Debriefing is questioning someone after a mission to extract information.

entries.clue: Catches son, acts the scold (5)

blocks.note: s = son, as in genealogies
to nag is to scold persistently

annotation.surface: A parent catches their son out and tells him off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Catches' looks like a verb about the son, and it is a verb, but in the sense of a sleeve snagging on a nail.
annotation.definitionFit: To snag is to catch on something sharp.

entries.clue: Monday rattled one that’s full of beans (6)

indicatorNotes.rattled: 'rattled' means shaken up, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

annotation.surface: Monday morning unsettles even the most energetic person.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Full of beans' is an idiom for energetic, not a literal tin of beans.
annotation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a tirelessly energetic person.

entries.clue: Place – place to drive from – place to park it? (6)

blocks.note: to place something is to set it down
in golf you drive off the tee

annotation.surface: A string of places: somewhere to set out, somewhere to start driving, somewhere to park the car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Park it' suggests a car after the drive, but it is slang for sitting down, as in 'park yourself'.
annotation.definitionFit: A settee is a sofa, where you park yourself.

entries.clue: Mustard on a roll, for a song (6,9)

blocks.note: mustard is a shade of yellow
a submarine is a long sandwich roll; 'on' puts mustard first

annotation.surface: Someone asks for mustard on a bread roll, perhaps in exchange for a song.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a snack order; the definition is just 'song', the 1966 Beatles hit.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Yellow Submarine' is a Beatles song.

entries.clue: Dubious treat, the eel’s dressed ‘skin’ (11)

indicatorNotes.Dubious: 'dubious' suggests something not right, the letters out of order
indicatorNotes.dressed: 'dressed' means prepared or arranged, as a salad is dressed

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: A suspicious dish: the eel has been served still in its skin.
annotation.walkthrough: The quote marks around 'skin' signal it is not real skin, and 'Dubious' reinforces that: leatherette is imitation leather.
annotation.definitionFit: Leatherette is fake leather, so a 'skin' in quotation marks.

entries.clue: Everyman’s given a drink at 4; from the outset, Everyman’s making things up (11)

indicatorNotes.from the outset: 'from the outset' means at the start, so take the first letter

blocks.note: the setter, Everyman, is 'I am', so I'M
used as is
gin is a drink
used as is
4 in Roman numerals
first letter of Everyman

annotation.surface: The setter gets a drink at four o'clock and starts inventing things.
annotation.walkthrough: '4' looks like a time or a cross-reference to 4 across, but it is the Roman numeral IV.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who invents freely has an inventive, fanciful mind.

entries.clue: A bounder, the writer describing European universities etc (7)

indicatorNotes.describing: to describe a circle is to draw around, so the pieces go around E

blocks.note: used as is
a bounder and a cad are both dishonourable men
the writer is the setter, ME
E = European

annotation.surface: A cad and a writer describe the universities of Europe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Describing' is the geometric sense, drawing a line around, as you describe a circle; it has nothing to do with writing.
annotation.definitionFit: A collective noun by metonymy: the academic world of universities, colleges and scholars.

entries.clue: Mo in no need of barista (7)

blocks.note: 'mo' is British slang for a moment, as in 'half a mo'
coffee made by just adding hot water, so no barista required

annotation.surface: Someone named Mo can make their own coffee without help.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mo' looks like a name, but it is short for moment.
annotation.definitionFit: An instant is a moment, and instant coffee needs only hot water.

entries.clue: Improved health for hubby? (5,4)

indicatorNotes.Improved: improving something changes it, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A wife hoping her husband's health will get better.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word, but its letters are needed in the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A husband is one's other half; the question mark admits it could be a wife too.

entries.clue: Counterpart of red – and of black? (5)

blocks.note: the other colour of wine
the opposing side in chess, or the other piano keys

annotation.surface: A question about opposites of colours.
annotation.walkthrough: Red's opposite number is white in wine, and black's is white in chess or piano keys.
annotation.definitionFit: White pairs with red in wine and with black almost everywhere.

entries.clue: One who wrote amusing novels such as Emma, you say? (9)

indicatorNotes.you say: 'you say' means as spoken, so go by sound

blocks.note: Emma Woodhouse is the heroine of Jane Austen's Emma

annotation.surface: A question whether Jane Austen's Emma counts as a comic novel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Emma' in italics is the novel, which points to Austen, but the wordplay wants its heroine's surname. P. G. Wodehouse wrote the comic Jeeves books.
annotation.definitionFit: P. G. Wodehouse was the great writer of comic novels.

entries.clue: Scrap fairy tale with king at the end becoming … dead (5)

indicatorNotes.becoming: 'becoming' says one thing turns into another, so K is swapped for D

blocks.note: Shrek is the animated fairy-tale film
K = king, the last letter of SHREK
d = dead, replacing K

annotation.surface: A plea to drop a fairy tale where the king dies at the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At the end' pins the king to the final letter of SHREK, which is then replaced. The ellipsis runs on into 20 down.
annotation.definitionFit: A shred is a scrap, a small torn piece.

entries.clue: Detective Inspector puts up with absence of intelligence (6)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, 'up' means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: DI = Detective Inspector
used as is

annotation.surface: A police inspector tolerates colleagues who lack brains.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Puts up with' reads as tolerates, but 'up' is doing its own job: DIPUTS turned around.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjectival phrase used as a plain synonym: lacking intelligence means dim or dull-witted.

entries.clue: What boots may be in a different case? (5,4)

annotation.definition: What boots may be in a different case?

blocks.note: the surface reading: footwear, lower-case boots
upper case: capitalised, Boots is the British chain of chemist's shops, a trade name

annotation.surface: A question about what boots might be in some other situation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A different case' means upper case: Boots with a capital is a British chain of chemist's shops.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: capitalising a common word can turn it into a company's trademark.

entries.clue: Heavy criticism, lawyers blow a fuse (7)

blocks.note: the bar is the collective body of barristers
to blow a fuse is to rage

annotation.surface: Lawyers lose their tempers under a storm of criticism.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface describes the lawyers reacting to criticism; in the wordplay they simply supply BAR.
annotation.definitionFit: A military term borrowed figuratively: a barrage of shellfire becomes a sustained torrent of complaints.

entries.clue: Number-cruncher: fastidious, proverbially patient type accepting unknown number (7)

indicatorNotes.accepting: to accept is to take in, so Y goes inside

blocks.note: anal = obsessively fussy
a saint, ST, has proverbial patience
algebra uses x, y, z for unknowns

annotation.surface: A fussy accountant, proverbially patient, taking on an unknown figure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The patience of a saint' is the proverb behind the saint here; 'accepting' takes the unknown into the gap between the first two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: An analyst is someone who crunches numbers.

entries.clue: Cockney’s cooking – then … ? (6)

indicatorNotes.Cockney’s: Cockneys drop their H's, so the H goes

blocks.note: heating food is cooking it; the Cockney drops the H

annotation.surface: A Cockney describes cooking, then asks what comes next.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the unfinished question: after cooking comes eating. A Cockney is a working-class Londoner, famous for dropping H's.
annotation.definitionFit: Eating is what naturally follows cooking.

entries.clue: How a list of Henry’s wives goes, excluding the final queen, OK? (2,2,3)

indicatorNotes.excluding: 'excluding' means leave out, so R is dropped

blocks.clueFragment: How a list of Henry’s wives goes
blocks.note: Henry VIII's six wives run from Aragon to Parr; the phrase ends at the last of them
R = queen (Regina), taken from the end

annotation.surface: Checking a list of Henry VIII's wives without the last one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The final queen' looks like Katherine Parr herself, the last wife, but it is R, the final letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A golfing idiom: par is the expected score, so meeting it means acceptable.

entries.clue: … piece of snipe with another bird (5)

indicatorNotes.piece of: a piece of something is part of it, so the answer sits inside

blocks.note: sniPE WITh

annotation.surface: Continuing from 15 across: a snipe and a second bird.
annotation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 15 across but plays no part here. 'Another' is fair because the snipe is also a bird.
annotation.definitionFit: The pewit, or lapwing, is a bird named for its call.

entries.clue: Component of lathe is twitching? I’m sceptical (7)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is something an atheist might say, standing for the person.

indicatorNotes.Component of: a component is a part, so the answer is part of the following words

blocks.note: lATHE IS Twitching

annotation.surface: Someone doubts that a twitching lathe part is anything to worry about.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the answer's voice: an atheist says 'I'm sceptical' about God.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by quotation: the answer is the person who would say this about God.

entries.clue: Understood, in a phrase, how a lip-reader describes her work (1,3,4,3,4)

annotation.definition2: how a lip-reader describes her work

blocks.note: the stock phrase for 'got it'

blocks.clueFragment: how a lip-reader describes her work
blocks.note: taken literally: she sees the meaning

annotation.surface: A lip-reader explains her job in a single phrase.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a phrase' tells you the answer is a spoken expression; the lip-reader half takes 'see' literally.
annotation.definitionFit: 'I see what you mean' is a way of saying 'understood'.

entries.clue: Location of unpleasantness on edge of eyelid? (4)

annotation.definition: Location of unpleasantness on edge of eyelid?

indicatorNotes.edge of: the edge of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a sty is a filthy pigpen
first letter of eyelid

annotation.surface: Asking where a nasty little swelling sits.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue both builds the answer and describes it: a stye is a sore swelling on the rim of the eyelid.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: the whole clue reads as a straight description of the eyelid swelling.

entries.clue: Falling over, run into swarm (4)

indicatorNotes.Falling over: something that falls over ends up the other way round

blocks.note: to run into someone is to meet them

annotation.surface: Someone tumbles over while running into a crowd.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run into' reads as a physical collision, but it means to meet by chance.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: things that teem swarm in great numbers.
